key_insight: The paper replaces the usual kinetic energy in optimal transport with Barron energy to define a neural-complexity-aware transport metric for generative modeling.
engineering_relevance: This gives a principled way to compare and design generative models by measuring how efficiently a neural network can implement a transport map or flow.
method: Start from Benamou–Brenier optimal transport and swap L2 kinetic cost for Barron energy.
Interpret the transport velocity as the function a neural hidden layer must represent.
Use the resulting metric to analyze diffusion models and adaptive feature-based transport.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports super-polynomial lower bounds on score approximation for data generated by neural-network pushforwards of a Gaussian, used to quantify diffusion model suboptimality.
watch_item: The framework is theoretical and relies on Barron-space assumptions, so practical gains depend on how well real models approximate these idealized complexity measures.
paper_title: Barron Optimal Transport I: Generative Modeling
